title: unit.v1
description: The DISPATCH — the one backend object (one run of an agent), composed of the seven primitives. The Scheduler fires it; the Runtime spawns an isolated container, mounts the granted workspace LIST + brokers creds; the Agent (runner) runs from a start point and streams on its derived Stream `unit:<id>:out`. The envelope carries WHO it acts for and who launched it (identity: subject · launcher · signed token), WHICH agent runs (runner), WHICH workspaces it mounts at what access (workspaces[{id,mode}] — mode is the write-access source of truth), WHICH tools it may call (tools — each auto|gate per its tool.v1 descriptor), WHY it fired (trigger — informs the DERIVED input-trust), what it is grounded in (context), and WHAT to do (start: an entry point or a resumed session). `trust` (all-ro && irreversible-gated) and `output` (`unit:<id>:out`) are DERIVED, never stored. There is no `lifecycle` — the Runtime reaps on idle and continuity is the session file in the workspace. No tenancy beyond subject (ADR-0003). Supersedes the flat MVP shape and the meeting-only invoke.v1.

Trigger.description: Why the dispatch fired — an input to the Scheduler, recorded for provenance + to DERIVE input-trust (message = you, in chat ⇒ trusted ⇒ rw; event/transcription from an external source ⇒ untrusted ⇒ propose-only). message = a user turn (chat, now); scheduled = a schedule entry fired (routine); event = an Integration published an event (e.g. email.received); transcription = a live transcript stream beat / session start (the in-meeting agent).

Mode.description: Workspace access mode — the SOURCE OF TRUTH for write access (governance). ro = materialized read-only; rw = synced back to the bucket on commit.

Workspace.description: One granted workspace mount: a workspace.v1 git-folder `id` (the store resolves it to a bucket location) + the access `mode`. A dispatch mounts a LIST — typically system (ro) + company (ro) + user (rw).

id.description: the workspace.v1 id (e.g. the subject for the personal workspace, or `system`/`company`)

Identity.description: The chain of custody. subject = the principal the agent acts ON BEHALF OF (data + quota owner). launcher = WHAT triggered this dispatch (the user, a schedule entry, or an Integration) — it must hold a signed delegation grant to act as the subject. token = the short-lived signed dispatch token (subject + launcher + scope) the Identity service mints; absent at author time, injected by the Runtime at spawn; every boundary verifies it, never the agent.

subject.description: identity.v1 subject = the PERSON = quota owner + cred-brokerage key (e.g. u_jane)

launcher.description: who/what triggered the dispatch, e.g. user:u_jane | schedule:<id> | integration:meetings

token.description: the minted short-lived signed dispatch token; injected at spawn, verified at every boundary

MeetingRef.description: Which meeting this dispatch is grounded in (context.kind=meeting) — referenced by id, never by importing meetings code (the meetings⊥agent boundary). The ids match transcript.v1; the agent consumes transcript.v1 by schema off `tc:meeting:{id}:mutable`.

SourceRef.description: An OPAQUE reference to a non-meeting context source (an email, a doc, a generic uri) that a tool resolves — never the bytes. Keeps email/calendar/tasks as Integrations, not platform domains.

uri.description: an opaque source uri, e.g. mailbox://user/INBOX/<id>

Context.description: What the dispatch is grounded in. `kind` is the discriminator; `none` is a bare chat with no external context. For a live meeting, `meeting` carries the ids the agent uses to consume the transcript stream.

EntryPoint.description: A fresh start: an inline ask (chat message / inline plan) and/or a workspace path to a plan doc. At least one of `inline` | `path`.

path.description: a workspace path to a plan doc, e.g. plan/morning-brief.md

SessionRef.description: A resumed start: a path to the agent's session file in the (rw) workspace. A fresh container resumes instantly from it — continuity is a file, not a warm container.

ref.description: a workspace path to the session file, e.g. .claude/.session

Start.description: What to do: EXACTLY ONE of an `entrypoint` (a fresh task) or a `session` (a resumed conversation).

Invocation.description: One dispatch. The dispatcher emits it (from any trigger source); the Scheduler fires it; the Runtime spawns it. `output` (= unit:<id>:out) and `trust` are derived, not stored.

runner.description: which agent CLI runner drives the turn (claude-code is the first; aider/others plug in)

workspaces.description: the granted workspace mounts (id + mode); mode is the write-access source of truth

tools.description: the scoped toolbelt (tool.v1 names); each resolves to auto|gate via its descriptor — the --allowedTools allow-set + the gate set

InputEntry.description: One entry of a live unit's input stream unit:<id>:in, where agent-api (its only writer) puts the person's next message for a warm worker. `turn` is the message as a JSON string; `sig` is HMAC-SHA256(key = the unit's input key, message = the `turn` string) as 64 lowercase hex digits. The unit key is HMAC-SHA256(INTERNAL_API_SECRET, "vexa-unit-input.v1:" + unit id), hex; agent-api derives it per unit and hands it to that unit's worker as VEXA_UNIT_IN_KEY, and no other worker holds it. A worker runs only entries whose signature holds under its key, and runs none when it has no key. The chat's pending list shows only verifying entries. A worker from v0.13.2 under an agent-api from before it finds every follow-up unsigned and drops it: upgrade agent-api and the worker image together.

InputVector.description: A unit-input vector: the unit key derived from `secret` and `unit_id` must be `key`, and signing `turn` with it must give `sig`. The secret is a fixture.

FaultSource.description: WHO failed (`Fault.source`). `runtime` — the agent runtime agent-api asks to start a worker (core/agent/shared/runtime_fault.py) · `model-provider` — the model's provider refused the turn (core/agent/llm/faults.py) · `vexa-tools` — the turn's Vexa tool access was refused (core/agent/worker/tool_access.py) · `agent-worker` — the worker would not start the turn in the environment it was given (core/agent/worker/tool_access.py, core/agent/llm/claude_code.py) · `agent-api` / `gateway` — the terminal's chat proxy got no typed answer from them (clients/terminal/src/app/api/chat/route.ts).

RuntimeFaultKind.description: spawn_refused — the runtime answered that it could not start the workload (runtime.v1 502, or 409) · quota_exceeded — the person's workload quota is full (429) · unauthorized — the runtime refused agent-api's caller credential (401/403) · refused — another 4xx · not_found — the runtime does not know the workload (404) · unreachable — no HTTP answer at all · unavailable — another server error · bad_response — a 2xx body that is not runtime.v1.

ModelProviderFaultKind.description: A provider call that failed: unpaid — out of credit or quota (402, or the provider's own words) · unauthorized — the credential was refused (401/403) · rate_limited — 429 · unavailable — 5xx, 529, a timeout or a transport failure · refused — any other 4xx. A chat's model pick that agent-api refused before any call (ADR-0043; `provider` is then the catalog's provider key and `model` the catalog id): unknown_model — not in the catalog · not_permitted — an admins-only model, for anyone else · not_configured — an own-endpoint model with no endpoint set, or a catalog offering this person nothing · credential_missing — the provider's secret_ref is not set · endpoint_refused — the person's own endpoint cannot carry the turn.

VexaToolsFaultKind.description: access_expired — the turn ran past its delegation token, and the Vexa tool calls it made after that were refused.

AgentWorkerFaultKind.description: tools_unconfined — a path the turn needs could not be handed to the user the model's tools run as, so the turn was not started (core/agent/worker/tool_access.py) · credential_conflict — the turn runs on the person's own model endpoint, and the worker's environment holds another model credential it could not remove, so the turn was not started (core/agent/llm/claude_code.py).

AgentApiFaultKind.description: internal — agent-api answered a 5xx with no typed fault · unavailable — it answered 502/503/504 with none.

GatewayFaultKind.description: unreachable — the terminal could not reach the gateway at all.

FaultRuntimeOp.description: Which runtime call failed (runtime faults only).

Fault.description: A dependency's typed failure (P18): WHO failed (`source`) and HOW (`kind`, closed per source — the `$def` named `<Source>FaultKind`), one safe sentence (`detail`) and what a person can do about it (`remedy`). Carried as `fault` on a failed `DoneFrame`, on an `ErrorFrame`, on a `DispatchRefusal`, and on a blocked inbox row. A runtime fault names its `op`; a model-provider fault names the `provider` host and the `model` ("" when unknown). `at` is present only on a fault agent-api recorded against a chat unit (`unit:<id>:fault`). The kind vocabularies are generated into every side that names one (`gen-faults.mjs`).

status.description: the dependency's HTTP status, or null when it gave none (a timeout, a refused connection)

detail.description: one safe sentence — never the dependency's raw text, never a secret

remedy.description: one line a person (or their operator) can act on, or ""

provider.description: model-provider only: the host the request went to, or "unknown"

model.description: model-provider only: the model id, or ""

at.description: a recorded fault only: when agent-api recorded it, in seconds since the epoch

DoneFrame.description: A turn's last UnitEvent on the worker's out-stream (`unit:<id>:out`), relayed unchanged to the chat stream. The frozen fields are `reply`, `sessionId` and `ok`; `fault` is additive. A `done` that carries a fault is a failed turn: `ok` is false, and `reply` is the fault as one sentence for a client that reads only the reply.

ErrorFrame.description: A chat-stream `error` frame: agent-api's relay answering an attach to a unit whose spawn failed, or the terminal's proxy answering for an upstream that gave no stream. `message` is the sentence an older client shows on its own.

DispatchRefusal.description: The JSON body agent-api answers a refused dispatch with — 503 when the runtime is down or full (`unreachable`, `unavailable`, `quota_exceeded`), 502 for every other runtime kind, never 500. `detail` stays a sentence for every client that reads only that; `fault` is the typed half.
